summary: Today’s pulse tracks Trump lawyers defend president banning journalists from White House ahead of court hearing – live, Ethiopia and Tigray accuse each of launching offensives, fuelling fears of new war, and Argentina’s Milei slams ‘useless’ UN at its summit, saying it ‘looked the other way’ over Falkland Islands - live. Across Guardian and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are trump, court, and first. In the background, Iran’s leader hits out at ‘bully’ Trump in UN speech but signals willingness to talk and Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years in prison for sexual assault keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Trump lawyers defend president banning journalists from White House ahead of court hearing – live
headlines.description: Trump lawyers say White House access is ‘a privilege, not a right’; CNN, Politico and MS Now to present case in court after president banned outlets from White House grounds “It was a short meeting, but it was a very important meeting,” Rubio said.

headlines.title: Ethiopia and Tigray accuse each of launching offensives, fuelling fears of new war
headlines.description: The local authorities reportedly seize Tigray's airports following reports of recent drone strikes.

headlines.title: Argentina’s Milei slams ‘useless’ UN at its summit, saying it ‘looked the other way’ over Falkland Islands - live
headlines.description: Argentinian leader says self-determination should not apply as ‘the population was implanted by the occupying power’ These latest attacks come just hours before Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s address to the UN general assembly, so he is likely to reflect on them during his UN speech later. So far, we have had no public comment from Zelenskyy or Ukraine’s foreign minister Andrii Sybiha.

headlines.title: Iran’s leader hits out at ‘bully’ Trump in UN speech but signals willingness to talk
headlines.description: Masoud Pezeshkian says Tehran is ‘ready for dialogue and diplomacy and negotiations but without the language of force’ Iran’s president, Masoud Pezeshkian, turned the tables on Donald Trump, describing America as the true bully and terrorist in the Middle East while also insisting that Iran had always shown a commitment to the negotiating table. In a defiant speech to the UN general assembly in New York, his first since the US and Israel launched an all-out war on Iran, Pezeshkian repeatedly vowed that Tehran would never bend the knee to America.

headlines.title: Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years in prison for sexual assault
headlines.description: In court, Miriam Haley said the assault had a "devastating effect on my life and sense of security that may never go away".

headlines.title: Germany pledges to phase out fossil fuels for first time with target of 2045
headlines.description: Campaigners say plan marks notable shift away from oil and gas as previously pledges were only for carbon neutrality Europe’s biggest economy, Germany, has committed to phasing out fossil fuels by 2045, despite fierce debate about its green policies. In a roadmap published on Wednesday , the German government set out for the first time an explicit promise of “transitioning away” from fossil fuels. Previous pledges were only for “carbon neutrality”.

headlinePool.title: Does Airtel Money mark the end of London’s listing drought? Not yet | Nils Pratley
headlinePool.description: The biggest flotation in five years was a bit of a shoo-in. Let’s see what happens when overseas competition is tougher Indian billionaire’s payments firm plots biggest London flotation in years A win is a win, but we should probably contain our excitement about the biggest flotation in London for five years . Airtel Money, a payments processor that operates in 13 African countries and should be worth between £6bn and £7bn, is a welcome addition to the stock market but it would be a stretch to say the event marks a definitive change in the weather to end the listings drought. Why? Because, in a sense, Airtel Money is already here. It is a 78%-owned subsidiary of Airtel Africa, an established FTSE 100 firm with a market value of £11.3bn ultimately controlled by Bharti Enterprises under the Indian billionaire Sunil Bharti Mittal , also known for his 25% stake in BT.

headlinePool.title: From cybersecurity to AI to Taiwan, what's at stake in Trump's summit with Xi
headlinePool.description: As President Trump and China's President Xi prepare to meet, Rush Doshi of the Council on Foreign Relations explains the current state of U.S.-China relations and what to expect from this summit.

headlinePool.title: UK politics: PM’s new anti-disinformation unit gets cross-party backing, as Farage declares it an attack on free speech – as it happened
headlinePool.description: Farage referred to the new unit and said Burnham was setting it up ‘using the excuse that Russia wants to interfere with elections’ The former Labour minister leading the government’s review into youth unemployment has written to 100 firms to ask them to provide work placements and jobs for young people, the Press Association reports. PA says: Alan Milburn , who was commissioned by former prime minister Keir Starmer to lead the government’s review into worklessness, has approached “business leaders” in sectors including rail, transport and utilities to ask them to provide more chances for young people. The Milburn review said Royal Mail, Octopus Energy, Greene King and Lloyds bank are among the companies who are already offering opportunities to school and university leavers. They are taking part in the review’s First Chance scheme, which has come from the review.

headlinePool.title: Iran's president tells Trump it will never 'bend the knee'
headlinePool.description: Masoud Pezeshkian's defiant speech to the UN comes after the US president threatened to "annihilate" Iran if a peace deal is not agreed soon.

headlinePool.title: Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years after sexual assault conviction
headlinePool.description: Sentencing comes after years of appeals and retrials in case involving former TV production assistant Miriam Haley Harvey Weinstein was sentenced to 15 years on Wednesday after being convicted of sexually assaulting former TV production assistant Miriam Haley in 2006 at his Manhattan apartment. Haley appeared in court on Wednesday morning and delivered a victim impact statement.

headlinePool.title: Watch: How toxic smog from wildfires is making Indonesians sick
headlinePool.description: Around 175,000 people in Indonesia have suffered from respiratory illness since August.

headlinePool.title: Unhappy couples staying put due to cost of living crisis, say divorce lawyers
headlinePool.description: Financial pressures suspected to be behind figures showing failed marriages are lasting longer in England and Wales Couples are putting off divorce because of the cost of living crisis, lawyers have said, after figures showed the average length of a marriage ending in divorce in England and Wales reached a record high last year. The Office of National Statistics (ONS) released figures on Wednesday showing that the average marriage ending in divorce in 2025 lasted for 13 years. This is the longest since records began in 1963 and up from a record low of 8.9 years in 1985.

headlinePool.title: Poland accuses Russian military helicopter of violating its airspace
headlinePool.description: Poland says the aircraft stayed in its skies for 42 seconds, forcing the Nato member to scramble its fighter jets.

headlinePool.title: Criminals recruiting students on social media to be ‘parcel mules’, say police
headlinePool.description: Organised crime groups offer cash to move packages containing drugs or weapons, says West Yorkshire force Students are being recruited by criminals to transfer illegal packages containing illegal drugs, prohibited weapons, stolen goods and dirty cash, say police in West Yorkshire. Organised criminals are using social media platforms including Snapchat, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook to recruit people to help them move illicit goods, particularly targeting students and vulnerable adults.
